themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks spiked to 7 this week versus a 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (1020% increase, z-score 5.74)—a statistically significant surge suggesting possible overcrowding, unsupervised gatherings, or lack of enforcement in Central Harlem's green spaces this week.
evidence: 7 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score 5.74)
1020% spike represents a statistically significant deviation (severity: high)
Pattern emerged in current week, not established trend
reporting_angles: Which parks are experiencing the noise complaints? Are specific parks (e.g., Marcus Garvey, St. Nicholas Terrace) being overwhelmed?
Is there a Parks Department or NYPD enforcement presence, or have budget cuts reduced monitoring?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 19 last week versus a 4.9 weekly average (290% increase, z-score 8.01)—a sharp spike indicating widespread pavement damage or hazards affecting pedestrian safety across Central Harlem.
evidence: 19 sidewalk condition complaints last week vs. 4.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score 8.01)
290% spike in this category suggests concentrated deterioration
Correlates with 441 DOB alteration permits filed (373 alteration projects), suggesting active construction may be damaging streets
reporting_angles: Are construction projects on West 124th Street, Frederick Douglass Boulevard, or other active ULURPs responsible for sidewalk damage?
Which neighborhoods within CD110 have the worst sidewalk conditions? Document with photos and resident complaints.

themes_detail.label: Litter and Posting Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests and illegal posting complaints each exceeded 1000% of their 8-week baselines last week (5 and 3 complaints respectively, z-scores 9.55 and 8.69)—a dramatic dual spike suggesting either a sanitation service failure or a coordinated spike in street littering and vandalism.
evidence: Litter Basket Request: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score 9.55, 1233% increase)
Illegal Posting: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score 8.69, 2300% increase)
Both spikes clustered in same week, suggesting correlated failure (sanitation crew absence, enforcement gap, or organized vandalism)
reporting_angles: Has the Sanitation Department reduced service or reassigned crews from Central Harlem? Check for workforce/budget changes.
Are illegal postings (posters, stickers, tags) concentrated in specific blocks or commercial corridors? Interview residents on which streets are most affected.

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Spike Two Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 7 two weeks ago versus a 0.6 weekly average (1020% increase, z-score 5.74)—a significant spike that peaked earlier than other sanitation issues, but has not been updated with current-week data to confirm if trend is ongoing or resolved.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score 5.74, 1020% increase)
Timing is older than current week spikes; unclear if issue is still active
Overlaps with timing of illegal posting spike, suggesting possible coordinated vandalism period
reporting_angles: Has graffiti cleanup occurred since 2 weeks ago, or is the problem still visible on streets?
Are specific neighborhoods or property types (e.g., MTA infrastructure, private buildings, municipal facilities) being targeted?

themes_detail.label: Drinking Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Drinking-related 311 complaints jumped to 3 last week versus a 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)—a notable spike that may signal increased public drinking, inadequate shelter capacity, or lack of police enforcement in parks and public areas.
evidence: 3 drinking complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score 6.35, 1100% increase)
Aligns with park noise spike (both occurring in same week), suggesting overlapping public safety concerns in open spaces
Community Board budget requests show 'Upgrade existing facilities for the homeless' as recurring ask, suggesting chronic service gaps
reporting_angles: Is the spike linked to insufficient shelter beds or outreach services? Cross-check with Department of Homeless Services caseloads.
Are complaints concentrated in specific parks (e.g., Marcus Garvey) or transit hubs? Map the geography of incidents.
